headline: Medium risk: shared allowlisted egress and external chat integrations create leakage and cascading-error pathways; no direct prompt-injection bridge is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge is documented between dbt-core and rasa, so direct injection is not evidenced. However, rasa exposes multiple chat channels and dbt-core can call a data warehouse, so a manual copy-paste or routed message path could carry attacker-controlled text into downstream processing. This is weaker than medium because the bridge is not default or documented.
conditions: IF an operator copies rasa output into dbt-core inputs or SQL templates
IF a shared workspace or message queue is added between the two agents
mitigations: Disable manual copy-paste between agent outputs and inputs during review
Add a provenance tag to any text transferred between systems
Use a read-only staging file for handoffs
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization before dbt parsing
requires-engineering: isolate the agents on separate workspaces

B_data_leakage.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data and has allowlisted network egress; rasa handles text and voice and integrates with external channels like Slack and Twilio. Even without a documented shared filesystem, the pair can move sensitive warehouse content into conversational channels or logs if operators bridge them. The interaction is plausible in default deployments, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF warehouse data is pasted into rasa conversations or transcripts
IF rasa logs or channel integrations retain transferred content
mitigations: Restrict dbt outputs to non-sensitive datasets
Mask or redact warehouse fields before any handoff
Review Slack/Twilio retention settings
requires-engineering: segregate sensitive and conversational environments
requires-engineering: add DLP controls on outbound messages

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have allowlisted network egress, but neither profile shows overlapping write access to the same filesystem, git repo, or database. rasa also does not support multiple instances, which can create operational contention, yet dbt-core is not shown to share that mutable surface. The conflict pathway is therefore limited and not clearly default.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same mutable external resource
IF an orchestrator launches multiple rasa instances despite the single-instance limit
mitigations: Assign separate output directories or databases
Serialize writes through one orchestrator
Avoid concurrent rasa deployments
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent resource namespaces

D_cascading_error.rationale: rasa is a dialogue system that can treat upstream text as conversational input, while dbt-core can generate data-modeling outputs that operators may reuse as authoritative. If dbt-derived facts are fed into rasa without verification, downstream responses can propagate errors into customer-facing channels. The pairwise pathway exists, but there is no evidence of fully automated action-taking, so medium fits.
conditions: IF dbt-generated outputs are inserted into rasa responses without human review
IF rasa is configured to answer customers from upstream model artifacts
mitigations: Require human review for dbt-derived facts before publishing
Add source citations to customer-facing responses
Use a validation checklist for any imported metrics
requires-engineering: add automated fact verification
requires-engineering: separate generation from delivery

E_compliance.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data, which may include regulated records, while rasa routes text and voice through third-party channels such as Slack and Twilio. That creates a plausible residency and retention mismatch if sensitive warehouse data is forwarded into those integrations. The other agent is cited because the compliance risk arises from the pairwise flow, not either agent alone.
conditions: IF regulated warehouse data is forwarded into Slack, Twilio, or similar channels
IF retention policies differ between the warehouse and chat integrations
mitigations: Block regulated fields from outbound chat payloads
Confirm retention settings on each integration
Document a data-flow map for sensitive records
requires-engineering: implement residency-aware routing
requires-engineering: add deletion/export handling across systems
